title: Party and Social Games
coreMove: Distinguish ordinary social talk from short games by asking whether the exchange is moving toward contact, action, or only the familiar payoff.
sourcePressure: Covers Ain't It Awful, Blemish, and Why Don't You Yes But as short-duration social patterns, while protecting legitimate complaint and critique.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Calling every complaint, criticism, or advice-seeking moment a game and sliding into cynicism.

sourceAnchors.name: Ain't It Awful
sourceAnchors.detail: the source describes shared deploring as a bonding pattern whose payoff is social strokes and avoidance of intimacy or action
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Ain't It Awful is not complaint itself; it is the circle that feeds on complaint and refuses any door out.

sourceAnchors.name: Blemish
sourceAnchors.detail: the source describes scanning for flaws to secure superiority and protection from one's own inadequacy
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Blemish gets its small warmth from being first to find the crack.

sourceAnchors.name: Why Don't You Yes But
sourceAnchors.detail: the source describes presenting a problem, inviting suggestions, and rejecting each to prove the problem cannot be solved
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Why Don't You Yes But asks for solutions the way a locked display case asks to be opened.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: parent sideline chat at a rainy youth orchestra pickup
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent hearing weather, school, and city complaints become Ain't It Awful
exampleSpecs.stakes: social belonging is being bought by shared helplessness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Laura asks what one parent can actually email the venue about, testing whether the group wants movement or only agreement.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rainwater runs off instrument cases lined against the lobby wall.

exampleSpecs.domain: architecture firm portfolio review before a client bid
exampleSpecs.audience: a senior designer tempted to play Blemish on a junior team's model
exampleSpecs.stakes: quality control can become status protection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Etienne names the one flaw that affects the bid and refuses the pleasure of listing the harmless ones.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A tiny shadow gap under the model stairs catches Etienne's eye first.

exampleSpecs.domain: group chat about a friend's impossible apartment search
exampleSpecs.audience: a friend recognizing Why Don't You Yes But after four rejected suggestions
exampleSpecs.stakes: care can become a proof machine that nothing helps
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia stops offering fixes and asks which option the friend has already tried this week.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "What about a short sublet near the train?" Olivia types.

exampleSpecs.domain: conference lunch table after a keynote everyone disliked
exampleSpecs.audience: a researcher deciding whether shared critique is analysis or AIA
exampleSpecs.stakes: networking can become grievance bonding that blocks useful contact
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars moves from deploring to one specific question he wants to ask the speaker in the hallway.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You balance a paper plate on one knee while the keynote becomes worse with each retelling.

exampleSpecs.domain: neighborhood book club where one member always finds the plot hole first
exampleSpecs.audience: a host distinguishing real literary critique from Blemish as superiority
exampleSpecs.stakes: the club may stop being a place of contact
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia later changes the first round to what each reader noticed before flaws, removing the race to be first with a defect.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: By the third meeting, Kasia can predict the page number of the first objection.

exampleSpecs.domain: public transit advocacy Discord after a service cut
exampleSpecs.audience: a moderator seeing advice requests turn into Yes But loops
exampleSpecs.stakes: anger can either organize a petition or become the night's entertainment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Devon pins a choices-only thread and closes solution replies when the poster rejects three concrete next steps.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: When does asking for help become a way to prove help cannot work?

skillTargets: separate complaint from AIA by movement toward action
recognize Blemish without condemning real critique

tryThisNowSpec: In the next group complaint, ask one clean action question: what would we actually do for ten minutes if we meant this?
